standards.name: Minimum Information About Somatic Mutation (MIASM)
standards.abstract: MIASM defines a minimum set of metadata to report cancer-related somatic sequence variations. The research objects are somatic variants observed in tumor samples, with associated information about the variant (genomic coordinates, reference/altered sequence, protein impact), the detection method, the tumor sample (topography, morphology, origin, grade/stage), patient demographics and clinical context, and study design. The standard (Olivier et al., 2009) was published/maintained by the original authors and is listed in the Biosharing portal; it targets researchers, clinicians, epidemiologists, database curators, bioinformaticians, journal editors and funders and provides field-level recommendations and preferred vocabularies (HGNC, RefSeq/LRG, HGVS, ICD-O-3, RECIST, etc.) to promote consistent annotation and data integration.

classification.rationale: The source material includes an explicit tabular specification (Olivier_Table2) listing named data attributes, inclusion level, and recommended standards/vocabularies for each attribute. This is a genuine metadata table with distinct fields and recommended formats/ontologies, so it should be extracted as a table.

Where the source specified a controlled vocabulary or examples, enum or ontology_term types were used; where a numeric unit was specified (months, years) integer was used.
